findings.text: Route surface is a hand-rolled Handle(...) bool chain with strings.Split segment matching (repeated len(parts) == 2 && parts[1] == "x" && method cases), which AGENTS.md explicitly forbids in favor of ServeMux method patterns; likewise map[string]any request/response shaping instead of typed wire DTOs — cohesive and well-ordered, but a real deviation from the documented architecture (one of the 13 ratchet-baselined routers).

New-episode filtering duplicated between checkNew and filterNew: both rebuild the same known-guid/known-url map and apply the same published <= after + limit loop, with divergent publishedAt type handling (float64-then-int64 vs switch) — the two live paths can drift.
trimOldestEpisode silently swallows file-removal failure (if err != nil { return nil }) — trim reports success and no DB cleanup runs, no log or event.

Silent-except cluster: newUUID() ignores ids.New() error (empty id on failure); startSchedules() sets h.scheduler = nil and silently disables all auto-download schedules if the startup query fails; serverSettings() swallows scan error and unmarshal, falling back to empty defaults with no logging.

durationSeconds ignores per-segment parse failures (fmt.Sscanf discarded) — a segment like "xx" contributes 0 while the position multiplier still advances, silently mis-computing durations for malformed itunes:duration.

Internal publishedAt/enclosure-length values checked as int64 then float64 in several places because parsed feeds are map[string]any while re-parsed DB JSON is float64 — type-dance artifact of the any-typed episode model.
